text: The case status and the officer task stay rwb-case's. The document-set step reports an outcome to the parent CaseWorkflow, which moves the case to OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER_DIL or AWAITING_CREDIT_APPROVAL and, on a refused or incomplete set, raises the officer task. No case, assignment or task table is read or written by rwb-treatment, and the case status used by AC2 and AC3 is supplied by the rwb-case contract mock.
why: Two of the four legacy acceptance criteria end with the case in a new state (OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER_DIL, AWAITING_CREDIT_APPROVAL) while Architecture v5 gives the case, its CMMN state, queues, tasks and timers to rwb-case and gives rwb-treatment no call to P3; DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables and no source states how a stage is told the case reached TRANSFER_PRICE_SET or WITH_FCR_OFFICER.

text: The party set of a treatment is read from the service's own read-only ACE view v_ace_customer (DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074): the request carries the party count and the party keys only, and no name, national identifier, address or document number is supplied by rwb-treatment. The merged personal values on a document body belong to the rendering engine of RWB-S2-E2026-APP and P5 rwb-document and are masked by policy. If the platform keeps the views to rwb-source-data, the read moves to that contract and a C dependency appears.
why: DP-05 allows either the contract read of rwb-source-data or the service's own views and the Work Package lists no C dependency, while the legacy data table of RWB-E3-018 names v_ace_customer with the party fields and no source states whether this service reads it or receives the party values from the engine.

text: The rendering of the set is RWB-S2-E2026-APP's generateContractDocument activity, which owns the one-hop call to the generation operation of the published RWB-P5-E2026-CON with its 2 s timeout, its breaker, its idempotency key, its error set and its fake. RWB-S2-E3018-APP composes the set, hands it over, checks the returned documents against the approved template version in force and records the outcome, so it publishes no REST call and records no C dependency, which is what the Work Package lists. The four document types and their template codes are catalogue values read at their version.
why: The Work Package records no C dependency and no DP-11 for this pair, the pattern list is DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19, and both the legacy data table and TSD S2 hand document, document_type and document_hub_parameter to the document module while the template catalogue is rwb-comms'; the treatment side of the rendering already exists as legacy RWB-E2-026 split into RWB-S2-E2026-APP and RWB-P5-E2026-CON.

text: The set answer is published as an optional documentSet section of the treatment answer of RWB-S2-E3001-CON at the same major version, with setStatus, composedAt, ruleId, ruleVersion, reasonCode and a documents array whose elements carry documentType, templateCode, templateVersion, documentId, docVersion and documentStatus. The stage hands over a DocumentSetRequest with the case and treatment references, the rule and version, and one entry per required type with its code, version and party count. The status vocabulary is COMPLETE, INCOMPLETE, REFUSED and UNMATCHED. The names, the example values and the error mapping are the working read; no table, no column and no code list is created by them.
why: No source gives the set a field, an element or an operation, and the legacy story lists only the treatment create and read, so the section and the request have to be published somewhere for four consumers to build against; the treatment read is the only published surface the officer's two screens already use.
